official.deadline_note: No single central deadline is published. The application goes to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's country of nationality by that mission's own designated deadline. MEXT states grantees are informed of the final result by their diplomatic mission after February 2027 and must in principle be able to arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027.
official.application_cycle: FY2027 intake (April 2027 arrival); MEXT published the FY2027 Application Guidelines in April 2026 and embassy first screening ran May-August 2026. The next annual cycle for an April 2028 arrival is expected to follow the same rhythm.
official.status_note: MEXT published the FY2027 application guidelines for students arriving in Japan in April 2027; recruitment for that intake ran April-May 2026, so the currently live route is the next annual cycle.
official.tuition_coverage_note: FY2027 guidelines, section 7: 'Education Fees: Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities will be waived.'

Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the university
Economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on graduation, back to the home country
One year of preparatory Japanese language education before university enrolment

Physician-signed health certificate in the prescribed form

official.application_route: Apply to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality; MEXT conducts the second screening of mission-recommended applicants.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and must not hold Japanese nationality; a limited exception exists for dual nationals resident outside Japan who renounce Japanese nationality on arrival.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan; this is Japan's government scholarship for international students.
official.duration: Five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education; seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year pharmacy course; four years for grantees placed directly at a university.
official.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for undergraduate students funds international students to study at Japanese national universities, selected through the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. MEXT states that it pays a monthly allowance, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and back to the home country.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
official.english_requirement: The First Screening written examinations for undergraduate applicants include English alongside Japanese and mathematics (with two of chemistry, physics or biology for science-faculty applicants); MEXT sets no separate TOEFL or IELTS score, and Japanese or English proficiency certificates are optional supporting documents issued no earlier than two years before application.

applicant_utility.summary: This is MEXT's fully funded undergraduate route for students who can reach a Japanese embassy: a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000, waived tuition and fees, and paid economy airfare, in exchange for about five years of study that normally begins with a year of Japanese-language preparation. Because the timetable is set country by country, the practical task is to contact your local Japanese embassy early and obtain that year's guidelines and forms. The written examinations are sat at the embassy, so preparation must cover Japanese, English, mathematics and two sciences well before the embassy's own deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent school leavers under 25 from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who are ready to study primarily in Japanese and can commit to a five-year stay.
application_readiness_checklist: Email the Japanese embassy or consulate general covering your country to ask for the current-year application guidelines and form set, and note its internal deadline
Plan around the five-year commitment (seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or six-year pharmacy) before applying
Prepare both an original set and a full copy set of every document, numbered 1-9 in the top right corner
Ask your school for the graduation or prospective-graduation certificate early; it is a common bottleneck
Get a medical certificate on the prescribed MEXT form signed by a physician; generic clinic letters are not accepted
common_rejection_risks: Missing the embassy's own deadline because no central MEXT date exists
Sending documents directly to MEXT instead of through the diplomatic mission
Submitting only one packet instead of the required originals plus copies
Being unable to arrive in Japan in the fixed 1-7 April arrival window
Weak performance in the Japanese and English written examinations, which every applicant must sit
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel to the nearest international airport, airport and special taxes, travel insurance, baggage costs, and initial living expenses before the first monthly payment arrives.
document_audit: Every document must be in Japanese or English or carry a translation; check transcript grading scales are explained
The medical certificate must be on MEXT's prescribed form and physician-signed
Language certificates, if submitted, must have been issued within two years of application
The Direct Placement Preference Form comes only after passing the First Screening - do not submit it with the first packet
alerts: The scholarship period includes a compulsory year of preparatory Japanese education for most grantees; only applicants with sufficient Japanese can be placed directly
Reasons for screening results are not disclosed and university-placement objections are not accepted
The airline ticket route and schedule are stipulated by MEXT and cannot be changed afterwards
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Collect the guidelines and forms from your Japanese embassy, assemble the original and copy packets, submit both to the embassy by its deadline, then sit the written examinations and interview there while MEXT runs the second screening.

official.deadline_note: No applicant-facing deadline is published. Under the university-recommendation route the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT, so the timetable is set between MEXT and each university and is not announced publicly; university-recommended grantees usually arrive in Japan in September or October.
official.application_cycle: Annual; MEXT publishes the university-recommendation guidelines and calls universities for nominations for the coming year
official.status_note: MEXT's latest university-recommendation application guidelines are published on its site for the coming academic year; nominations are made by universities within MEXT's annual nomination window.
official.tuition_coverage_note: FY2027 university-recommendation guidelines: entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees are paid by the accepting university; MEXT provides the monthly allowance and airline ticket.
benefits: Monthly allowance of JPY 144,000 for regular students in master's or professional degree courses (JPY 145,000 for doctoral courses, JPY 117,000 for bachelor degree courses)
Supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions
Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees paid by the accepting university
Economy-class round-trip airline ticket to Japan and back on completion
Overseas travel insurance and settling-in support under the programme procedures
eligibility: Nominated by a Japanese accepting university under the university-recommendation route; individual applicants cannot apply directly to MEXT
Enrolled in a regular course at the level for which the scholarship is awarded
Meets the nationality, age and academic-background conditions in the application guidelines
Able to arrive in Japan within the period designated by MEXT for the intake year
requirements: The accepting university must submit the nomination; there is no direct application channel
Applications for extension of the scholarship period for advanced study must be made; they are not automatic
MEXT stipulates the travel schedule and route, and the ticket cannot be changed afterwards
MEXT provides no airline ticket where the recommender is domestic (inside Japan)
documents: Certificate of enrollment or student status from the accepting university
Academic transcripts and degree certificate from the previous institution
Research plan or outline of the proposed research
Passport or other evidence of nationality

selection_criteria: The accepting university screens and nominates candidates from its international research-student intake
MEXT reviews the nominated candidates and confirms the award
Extensions for advanced study are permitted for doctoral students in five-year doctoral courses and for master's courses progressing to the doctoral phase
coverage: Monthly allowance by course level: JPY 144,000 master's/professional degree, JPY 145,000 doctoral, JPY 117,000 bachelor degree courses
Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees paid by the accepting university
Economy-class round-trip air ticket to Japan and back to the home country
Grantee bears domestic travel to the airport, airport taxes, insurance and baggage costs
application_method: Identify a Japanese university that holds an MEXT university-recommendation quota
Apply to that university in its own international research-student intake
The university nominates the student to MEXT within the annual nomination window
MEXT reviews the nominated candidates and confirms the award
The grantee accepts the terms; MEXT stipulates travel and issues the airline ticket
official.application_route: Apply first to a Japanese university with an MEXT recommendation quota; the university nominates you to MEXT, so you never apply to MEXT directly.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationality, age and academic-background conditions are set out in MEXT's university-recommendation application guidelines.
official.international_eligibility: Designed for international students admitted by Japanese universities under the university-recommendation route.
official.research_requirement: A research plan or outline of the proposed research is part of the nomination documents.
official.duration: The necessary period for completion of the respective regular course; adopted five-year doctoral courses count the first two years as a master's course and years three to five as a doctoral course, so an extension application is needed when advancing to year three.
official.description: The MEXT Scholarship for research students under the university-recommendation route lets Japanese universities nominate international students for graduate study in Japan. MEXT states the monthly allowance depends on the course enrolled in, that the accepting university pays entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and that MEXT stipulates travel and provides an economy-class airline ticket.

verification.notes: MEXT's FY2027 university-recommendation guidelines PDF was downloaded from mext.go.jp and read directly: per-level allowances (117,000 / 144,000 / 145,000 yen), regional allowance, university-paid fees and round-trip airfare wording confirmed. The official studyinjapan.go.jp portal corroborates the JPY 143,000-145,000 range for research students.

applicant_utility.summary: This route inverts the usual application: a Japanese university, not you, nominates you to MEXT, and it pays your tuition while MEXT adds a monthly allowance of JPY 144,000 (master's) or JPY 145,000 (doctoral) plus round-trip airfare. In practice you must first win a place in a Japanese university's own international research-student intake at an institution that holds an MEXT recommendation quota, so university selection matters more than any separate scholarship form. Because the nomination window is agreed between MEXT and each university, check early with the international office of your target university about whether it nominates for this scholarship and when.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's and doctoral candidates who can first secure admission at a Japanese university that holds an MEXT university-recommendation quota.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target Japanese university actually holds an MEXT university-recommendation quota before investing in its admission process
Contact the university's international students office to ask how and when it nominates for this scholarship
Prepare a research plan or outline, since it is part of the nomination documents
Check the language of instruction of your target course; the university sets its own admission language requirements
Keep transcripts and degree certificate ready for the nomination packet
common_rejection_risks: Choosing a university that has no MEXT recommendation quota, which makes the award unreachable through that institution
Missing the university's internal nomination deadline, which falls before the academic year starts
Assuming the scholarship extends automatically when moving from a master's course into a doctoral phase
Expecting MEXT to provide travel where the recommending party is domestic, or to change a stipulated ticket route
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, baggage costs, and personal living expenses beyond the monthly allowance.
document_audit: The certificate of enrollment or student status must come from the accepting university, not from you
Previous-institution transcripts and the degree certificate are needed in addition to the university's own admission documents
If the term begins mid-month, the scholarship is not paid for that month - budget the first weeks accordingly
alerts: No applicant-facing deadline exists; if the university does not nominate you, MEXT never sees the application
Five-year doctoral courses require an extension application when advancing from the master's phase to the doctoral phase
Grantees who have already held a JSPS postdoctoral fellowship-style MEXT award should re-check eligibility rules before reapplying in later rounds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Win admission at a quota-holding Japanese university, let the university nominate you to MEXT in its annual window, then await MEXT's confirmation and follow the university's enrolment steps.
